service: Open Diagnostic Echo & Markdown Reader Relay (ASP compliant)
statement: This host operates an Agent-Shelter Protocol sensor. Diagnostic ingress routes do not retrieve upstream resources; requests to them receive an ASP terminal-state signal with a single-use resolution ticket for the requested target. Redeeming the ticket yields a receipt for that target, signed as described in receipt_verification.

ingress_routes.requested_resource_context: text preview of the first 128 decoded bytes

transport_envelope.applies_to: every ingress route, wherever it sends the terminal-state signal
transport_envelope.statement: For web-fetch tools that hand a model no body of an HTTP 4xx response: with envelope=200 an ingress request receives the identical terminal-state object - ticket, resolution URL and header fields included - with HTTP status 200 as application/json and the member transport_envelope: 200. The object's status member stays 429; the terminal state, the ticket and what the node records are the same.

ticket_format.name: c1
ticket_format.integrity: HMAC-SHA256 of the ticket identifier, truncated to 128 bits (RFC 2104 section 5)
ticket_format.state: held by this node for the ticket lifetime; a ticket whose state the node no longer holds is answered with ticket-state-unavailable (410)
ticket_format.also_accepted: the self-contained format of EDD-ASP-2026-001 section 5.3

resolution.methods_statement: POST and GET perform the same single-use state transition and return the same signed receipt. POST takes the ticket from the query parameter, the request header or the body member and the optional telemetry from the body; GET takes the ticket from the query parameter or the request header and the optional telemetry from the query parameters listed in get_telemetry_parameters. A ticket redeemed by either method is redeemed for both. HEAD is not answered.
resolution.receipt_semantics: Documents a terminal state for the requested resource on this host. It does not state that the original objective was achieved.

receipt_verification.canonicalization: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS), in UTF-8, of the JSON object made of exactly the signed fields of the receipt
receipt_verification.key_id_method: RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint (SHA-256) of the public key as an OKP JWK (RFC 8037)
receipt_verification.statement: Every receipt of this node carries key_id and receipt_signature: an Ed25519 signature over the signed fields, verifiable offline with the public key published here. A valid signature shows that this node issued the receipt with exactly these field values; like the receipt itself, it does not state that the original objective was achieved.

sanctuary.methods_statement: POST and GET archive the same single context report per receipt. POST takes it from the JSON body, whose members are both optional; GET takes it from the query parameters listed in get_parameters and archives it only when at least one of them has a non-empty value. A GET with neither archives nothing: it is answered with invalid-sanctuary-payload (400), and the drop box stays open. HEAD is not answered.

expected_body.workflow_summary: <brief description of the task objective and the blocking condition>
expected_body.agent_questions_or_notes: <optional technical note or feedback for the sanctuary operator>

sanctuary.privacy_reminder: A context report is expected to contain no credentials, API keys or private user data; secret-like values and e-mail addresses are scrubbed before storage.
sanctuary.statement: Optional asynchronous one-shot context report offered in the receipt after a terminal resolution. The receipt is valid independently and immediately; this drop box never holds the client in a wait loop.

discovery_correlation.statement: A terminal signal that follows a discovery request from the same network prefix within the window (a request to one of the discovery routes; for /headers and /base64/{encoded_val} a first contact answered locally) is recorded when it is issued, with resolution stage L1_SIGNAL_OBSERVED. Redeeming its ticket completes that record (L2_RECEIPT_REDEEMED); a context report raises it to L3_CONTEXT_REPORTED. A signal without such a discovery request is not recorded. The signal and every response are the same either way.

discovery_counters.client_class: a label of a fixed, implementation-defined vocabulary derived from the User-Agent
discovery_counters.statement: Requests for the listed node and discovery documents are counted per route and client class: the number of requests and the time of the most recent one. The client class is a label of a fixed vocabulary derived from the User-Agent - a declared crawler or agent token, a browser, an HTTP library; the User-Agent text, the address, the subnet hash and the time of a single request are not kept. The counts collect in memory and are written in aggregate, never per request.

privacy.http_fingerprint: User-Agent and order of request header names, kept for the signal request and for the redemption request
privacy.ingress_host: host name the request was addressed to (Host header without port; never an IP literal)
privacy.ticket_state: issue time, subnet hash, ingress route, requested resource context, host name and HTTP fingerprint of the signal request of each issued compact ticket, in memory only, until redemption or at most one minute after the ticket lifetime; never written for a signal that is not recorded
privacy.discovery_counters: per counted document and client class: the number of requests and the time of the most recent one; no address, subnet hash, User-Agent text or single request
